description: Broad proof targets with incremental certified component evidence. An in-progress target is not fully certified. Paths are repository-relative.

proofs.title: Reachable-state invariant preservation
proofs.statement: Every permitted transition preserves a meaningful invariant from valid initial/reachable states.
proofs.progress_note: Actual finite node traces preserve state and prior bindings; mixed live file/node traces including refusal, known abort and recovery preserve the phase/history relation. Provenance, complete runtime guards and physical refinement remain open. BP joint durable/pending sender binding and fixed-Store receiver state/context/decision invariants now hold through actual transitions and arbitrary finite replay; changing-Store composition remains open.

proofs.title: Atomic allocation and stable numbering
proofs.statement: Acceptance publishes all intended local memberships together and never reuses an allocated number for another article.
proofs.progress_note: Atomic logical publication and stable number/binding lemmas; persistent/reclamation integration remains open.

proofs.title: Identity and idempotent acceptance
proofs.statement: Retrying an accepted identity preserves its binding and introduces no duplicate allocation or obligation.
proofs.progress_note: Exact logical identity bindings and retries covered; native identities, signatures, and durable protocol retry path remain open.

proofs.title: Reservation and release safety
proofs.statement: Accepted obligations are accounted for and discharge requires the specified predicate over committed authorized evidence.
proofs.progress_note: Finite abstract admission and general release preserve valid ledgers; release preserves independent pins and known identities. Authorized/committed evidence validation, durable node release, and physical-byte charging remain open.

proofs.title: Codec and identity preimages
proofs.statement: Accepted values round-trip; deterministic encodings and domain-separated preimages have the specified uniqueness and version boundaries.
proofs.progress_note: Primitive and full schema-0 value round trips and accepted-input canonicality are certified. Exact article source preservation remains checked. An independent cbor2 6.1.4 run passed 38 cases. Native/batch/signature schemas and domain-separated preimages remain open. Experimental BP request/receipt ADU roundtrip and exact accepted-input canonicality are also certified, without selecting D01/D09. D01 was subsequently selected by the user for exact authored source bytes and separate projections; native encoding/preimage proofs and D09 remain open.

proofs.title: NNTP framing independence
proofs.statement: Parsing valid octets in different socket partitions yields the same events; dot-stuffing round-trips the specified domain.
proofs.progress_note: Fixed-mode framing composition, production event-yield preservation and exact consumed-prefix/suffix accounting are certified. Wildmat DP matches independent anchored semantics. Session-sensitive mode changes and complete protocol/effect refinement remain open. The served path is now the subject: books/served states partition independence of fn-served-step and of the whole reply stream, which is the function tools/run_reader.py calls once per socket read, so the wire pending_subject note is closed for framing. The concurrent server (books/owner) still does not certify.

proofs.title: Conditional crash recovery
proofs.statement: Under the disk model, recovery retains acknowledged commits, may retain complete unacknowledged commits, and exposes no partial transaction.
proofs.progress_note: Arbitrary mixed live/file traces including refusal/abort preserve exact ready-state replay and prior acknowledged records, conditional on the kernel crash model. Observed-image opening uses actual recovery with no fabricated acknowledgements or barriers; zero through four barriers remain gated, the fifth opens ready. Host adoption passed the integrated suite; physical byte correspondence, freshness and platform qualification remain separate from these targeted proofs. Receiver logical replay now preserves exact contexts and committed receipt ADUs against a fixed Store. Five actual receiver process-death cuts passed in the 133-test suite; process death is separate from power loss and general FNWF/FNRJ byte/live/replay refinement. Fencing, barrier and retention keystones are unchanged in statement and now run with the whole-state recognizers off the executable path (24 calls to 0 in the store cluster, 10 to 0 in core), carried under mbe instead. Real process evidence: the deploy gate SIGKILLed the server inside an open POST and the acknowledged article reread byte-for-byte after recovery. Byte-level torn writes remain the DESIGN-crash-model-v2 design, which is review finding D4.

proofs.title: Checkpoint equivalence
proofs.statement: Checkpoint plus suffix recovery preserves the required logical state of full committed-history replay.
proofs.progress_note: Logical capture stores the exact prefix node; restore runs the actual suffix loop without prefix input. General admissible-split equivalence includes consumed allocator gaps and final frontier normalization. Physical encoding/publication/generation selection and freshness remain open.

proofs.title: Compaction and protected closure
proofs.statement: Reclamation and crash-interrupted compaction preserve every dependency rooted by policy and obligations.

proofs.title: Index soundness and completeness
proofs.statement: Concrete/rebuilt indexes correspond to authoritative state, including all required range-query results.
proofs.progress_note: A derived group/local-number/message-id list is sound and complete against source memberships; its independent query agrees with authoritative source range enumeration for rebuilt indexes. The malformed public query refuses. Host adoption, persistent representation and indexing performance remain open.

proofs.title: Validated fact-set merge
proofs.statement: Under fixed validation hypotheses, immutable fact-set merge is associative, commutative, and idempotent; incomplete input has no complete-acceptance effects.
proofs.progress_note: Admissible ingest and arbitrary policy-changing traces preserve state and conflicting facts. Capacity-limited admission is intentionally not order-independent. Transfer staging correctness/work is proved separately; persistent progress, dependency authority, portable batches and receipts remain open. The merge and staging keystones are unchanged. Two-peer convergence is the K3 seam of DESIGN-peering-summary and is stated in no book.

proofs.title: Conditional responsibility handoff
proofs.statement: Sender discharge requires committed evidence of a matching successor undertaking under the cooperative-peer model.
proofs.progress_note: Certified sender finite traces preserve state, exact node and joint durable/pending work binding; transport traces preserve recorded receipts. Receiver actual record/replay transitions preserve typed context/Store/receipt relations against a fixed Store, require matching committed journal decisions for receipt emission, and retain byte-identical existing receipt ADUs. Real BP return and five receiver process-death cuts have separate test evidence under trusted local policy. General journal byte/live/replay and host refinement, receiver composition with Store evolution, authenticated cooperative-peer handoff and physical durability remain open; no complete handoff theorem is claimed.

proofs.title: Authority and provenance confinement
proofs.statement: Signatures, unknown schemas, legacy headers, and replays confer only authority allowed by recorded policy.
proofs.planning_note: D01 now fixes exact authored source signatures versus separate mutable trace/gateway projections. C1-11 and C2-02/03 must prove authority confinement for that boundary under explicit D09 verification/policy assumptions. No theorem completion follows from this design choice.

proofs.title: Guard and execution correspondence
proofs.statement: Guard-verified concrete operations used by the host implement their logical counterparts on the stated domains.
proofs.progress_note: Composed storage host adoption passed the 75-root/67-test batch. Seventeen existing base graphs now have 678 guarded functions, adding NNTP115 and semantic fields30 with unchanged existing logic; the derived index separately has 20 guarded functions. NNTP retains one explicit EC-CALL for total wildcard behavior. The host uses interpreted ACL2; full physical byte/effect correspondence and platform qualification remain open. The complete 41-function BP ADU codec now has verified guards after closing five streaming decoder functions without logical changes. An actual seven-book BP inventory records 97 functions still awaiting guard verification outside that codec; those remain a separate execution gap. The host's :program-mode chunk loop and its duplicate reply framing are gone: books/served owns both, in logic mode with guards verified. host/scheduler-host.lisp is still :program mode, and books/owner -- the host of the real service -- does not certify, so no run executes the proved core through the service entry point.

proofs.title: NNTP session refinement
proofs.statement: Session transitions implement the audited command-specific cursor, error, and publication rules.
proofs.progress_note: Actual implemented command/step and arbitrary finite raw event traces preserve session/cursor consistency under a valid archive projection. All dispatcher branches produce typed reply octets/close effects; closed sessions emit none. Exact bridge partitions and reconnect cases pass targeted tests. Full RFC responses/READER bundle, injection/POST and effects-to-I/O refinement remain open. fn-served-step and fn-served-run preserve the connection and type their effects, over the same fn-nntp-step the session keystones are about; the w5/legacy-commands branches (XOVER, HDR/XHDR, LIST HEADERS/ACTIVE.TIMES) are covered by the unchanged statements of fn-nntp-step-effects-well-formed and fn-nntp-step-preserves-consistent-session. Open: NNT-001's capability/dispatch mismatch, and the owner.

proofs.title: Bounded parsing and staging
proofs.statement: For the resource profile, parsing and modeled staging terminate within declared length, nesting, allocation, and work bounds.
proofs.progress_note: Article/UTF-8/wildmat output recognizers and DP correspondence are certified. Whole matcher work has a value-corresponding polynomial bound; public transfer missing-range work has a hypothesis-free bound covering malformed validation, structural label equality, lookup and traversal. These declared operation costs exclude numeric bit complexity/runtime allocation. Other parser work, peak allocation and physical capacity remain open. Complete public article parsing now has unconditional exact value correspondence and structural-work input/profile bounds, including malformed inputs and repeated folds. This closes the article parser traversal-cost gap, not peak allocation or runtime costs. The served fold's step count is bounded by the chunk length, so a socket read of n octets cannot drive an unbounded number of NNTP steps. The pessimistic number, with its scope: the closed-form work ceiling of the public article parser is roughly 16,000x the measured traversal cost of that same parser (tests/evidence/2026-09-18-article-work.md); it is an instrumented shadow, not a host measurement.

proofs.title: Origin sequence non-reuse
proofs.statement: Within the specified restore/incarnation discipline, different events cannot silently share an origin/incarnation/sequence identity.

proofs.title: Conditional delivery progress
proofs.statement: The scheduling/transport model progresses obligations only under explicit eventual-contact, capacity, route, and retry assumptions.
proofs.planning_note: Scheduled in the active disconnected path (C2-06 scheduler, C3-03 conditional progress), rather than waiting for a mission-profile milestone. This changes sequencing only; target remains planned with no theorem evidence. A-FAIRNESS and validated-transfer/handoff dependencies remain explicit.

proofs.title: Statement field codec canonicality (S1-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-field-round-trip: a well-formed statement whose base64 detached encoding fits the 8192-octet field bound decodes back to exactly its own header and signature; fn-stx-field-accepted-input-is-canonical: every accepted field value has exactly one canonical form, so a middle box cannot produce a second value that decodes to the same statement.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: Events are generated and their book `books/stx-carrier` is certified, but the statement of the target is wider than what has certified: `fn-stx-field-round-trip` and `fn-stx-field-accepted-input-is-canonical` are in `books/stx-invariants`, which errors on `dev` `52eb0db` because `books/stx-verify` is open at `fn-stx-decimal-octets-are-printable`. Stays `in-progress`. Note also that section 6 of the design states `fn-stx-field-accepted-input-is-canonical` over a free `payload` and is FALSE as written; the book states the payload-free form over `fn-stx-header-value-parts`, which is what the field actually carries.

proofs.title: The verdict is computed from the statement's own octets (S2-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-verified-implies-signature-over-own-octets: a :verified verdict is backed by a key named in this node's own keyring, a signature check over the statement's own signing preimage, and a ref recomputed from the receiver's projection of the received bytes; the companion fn-stx-transit-verdict-is-fn-stx-verdict equates the verdict recorded by fn-peer-transfer, the function the host calls on a TAKETHIS body, with that subject.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: Two things keep this `in-progress`, and only one is certification. (1) `books/stx-verify` is open at one form. (2) The subject rule is unmet even when it closes: the statement covers the verdict on the transit path, and `fn-stx-transit-verdict-is-fn-stx-verdict` names `fn-peer-transfer`, so it needs the peering K1 path before any certified theorem is about the function a host calls.

proofs.title: Transit merge: ids are the union (S3-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-transit-ids-are-union: after a durably completed transit acceptance the ids of the node's lace are exactly the union of the ids it held and the ids of the delta. Corollary of fn-lace-merge-ids-are-union; the proof event is the bridge lemma fn-stx-lace-of-accept-is-merge, which equates accepting a transit article with a singleton lace merge.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `tests/acl2/stx-transit-tests` CERTIFIES since w10/substrate-2, so the S3-1 witnesses have now RUN; before that they were written and unexecuted.

proofs.title: Equivocation is detected at the merge and recorded (S3-2)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-transit-equivocation-is-detected: two distinct statements sharing a (creator, incarnation, sequence) slot make the creator an equivocator in the merged lace and both forks remain members, so neither fork is dropped; fn-stx-reissue-detected-after-peering is its two-node form under an explicit distinct-content-id hypothesis, and fn-stx-equivocation-record-agrees-with-lace licenses the durable (:equivocation ...) record as a twin of the lace rather than a second authority.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `tests/acl2/stx-transit-tests` CERTIFIES since w10/substrate-2, so the S3-2 fork witnesses have now RUN.

proofs.title: The statement index is a proved twin (S3-3)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-index-agrees-with-lace: under the carried index invariant the index answers lookup and the equivocator question exactly as the linear fn-stx-lace projection; fn-stx-index-invariant-preserved-by-accept: acceptance preserves that invariant, so the projection is a proof-level object and never runs per served command (D3).
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `books/stx-index` CERTIFIES (w10/substrate-2). The three agreements `fn-stx-index-bindings-agree`, `fn-stx-index-slots-agree` and `fn-stx-index-equivocators-agree` are the keystones; `fn-stx-index-agrees-with-lace` is their `:rule-classes nil` corollary and is cited as such, and `fn-stx-recorded-equivocation-agrees-with-lace` is a corollary of that. Not closed: no host line calls `fn-stx-index-lookup` or `fn-stx-index-equivocatorp` -- `fn-node-statep` has no index slot -- so the theorem-subject rule is not met and the D3 claim is about a query the served path does not yet carry.

proofs.title: Transit admission is the policy function, and a peer cannot widen it (S4-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-transit-admit-is-fn-pol-admitp: the authority gate on the transit path is fn-pol-admitp over this node's lace and keyring, which is the theorem-subject equation for every policy theorem; fn-stx-peer-batch-cannot-change-policy: if a contact batch contains no statement by the group's authority verified under the local keyring, the policy in force is equal before and after the batch.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `tests/acl2/stx-transit-tests` CERTIFIES since w10/substrate-2, and the S4-1 witnesses were VACUOUS until it did: the hostile batch's delta was empty because the policy statement's carrier article had a prose body where `fn-stx-payload-for` projects base64. Both carriers are repaired and the deltas are now pinned by their own assertions.

proofs.title: Reconnection never revises admissibility (S5-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-commits-of-batch-are-verified-and-well-formed is the carrier obligation and the new work: under a well-formed keyring the commits a batch contributes are well formed and each has a verified statement behind it. On it rest fn-stx-reconnect-never-revises-admissibility, which keeps every fn-me-decide equal across the merge, and fn-stx-reconnect-exposes-the-partition, which makes two commits off a shared base a visible fork rather than a winner.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `books/stx-epochs` CERTIFIES (w10/substrate-2), so the carrier obligation `fn-stx-commits-of-batch-are-verified-and-well-formed` is proved and the three reconnection rows follow it as labelled corollaries of the `books/membership-epochs-invariants` keystones. Its local witness lemma needed a repair, not a weakening: `fn-stx-commits-of-lace-have-witnesses` asked only `fn-lace-p` of the delta and was false; it now asks that every statement of the delta verifies, which `fn-stx-batch-delta` satisfies by construction. Not closed: nothing on the host's reconnection path calls `fn-stx-commits-of-batch`, and A-CRYPTO stands behind every verification here.

proofs.title: The reader's verdict is the recorded verdict, three-valued (S6-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-reader-verdict-is-the-recorded-verdict: HDR :fn-verified renders the verdict acceptance recorded for the article and does not recompute it per query; fn-stx-reader-verdict-is-typed: the rendered value is always a member of *fn-stx-verdicts*, so :unverified and :absent never collapse into one token.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.

proofs.title: The two durable kinds are one sequence-ordered stream (R5)
proofs.statement: fn-cstr-merge-keeps-every-config-record and fn-cstr-merge-keeps-every-article-record: the merge of the configuration-record file and the transaction journal by the sequence field each record carries holds exactly the records of each file, in order -- the left side walks the merge, the right side walks the input file. fn-cstr-merge-is-sequence-ordered: two sequence-ordered files merge to one sequence-ordered stream, so the two-directory layout loses no ordering information. fn-cstr-ok-merged-replay-ends-in-a-configured-node: a merged replay that reports :ok ends in a fn-cnode-statep state, which carries reserved <= capacity, so every configuration record in the history was admitted at a node that had already replayed the article records before it. Covered scope: finite histories of the two record kinds; no on-disk interleaving is claimed.
proofs.progress_note: books/config-stream certifies (ACL2 8.7, persvati, 2026-09-20). The separating witness in tests/acl2/config-stream-tests is the argument for the decision: one (:set-capacity 1) over a history whose two articles reserve 2, which the configuration-only replay the host runs today accepts and the merged replay refuses with :config-refusal; a raise and a decrease to exactly the reservation total are both admitted, so the merged replay is not refusing every decrease. Open: the host still replays configuration first (specs/reconfiguration.md section 8).

proofs.title: What a configuration generation serves (R5)
proofs.statement: fn-cstr-created-group-is-served-exactly-from-its-generation: a group created by the delta that produces generation g is live at every generation from g on and at none below it -- both directions, so a connection pinned below g must not see it. fn-cstr-retired-group-is-served-exactly-below-its-generation: a group retired at g is live exactly at the generations from its creation up to g, and the entry, its stamp and its watermark stay (NNT-006). fn-ocfg-open-pins-the-live-configuration: under the state relation fn-ocfg-statep, an open that installs a connection at the identifier the owner was about to allocate gives that connection the owner's LIVE configuration as its pin -- the two hypotheses are fn-ocfg-statep and that the open was not refused. fn-ocfg-advance-observes-the-live-configuration: under fn-ocfg-statep, a connection that survives its advance is re-pinned to the live configuration -- the two hypotheses are fn-ocfg-statep and that the advance kept a connection at that identifier. fn-ocfg-pin-is-stable-without-advance: over an arbitrary finite event list holding no (:advance id) and no (:close id), a pinned connection keeps the configuration it opened at -- the hypotheses are that it has a pin and that the list re-pins nothing for it. fn-ocfg-list-active-lists-the-pinned-served-table: for an open connection, LIST ACTIVE renders the group names of the PIN's generation and never the allocation domain. Covered scope: one delta over a typed configuration value for the two fn-cstr theorems; for the four fn-ocfg theorems, the owner paired with a pin table whose domain the recognizer fixes to the open connections, over the owner's own events. NOT covered: no host line calls any fn-ocfg- function, so none of the four has the equating theorem the assurance rules ask for; the served port still answers LIST ACTIVE from the allocation domain, which is the R5 wire seam recorded at the end of books/owner-config.lisp and in specs/reconfiguration.md section 8.
proofs.progress_note: books/config-stream certifies (ACL2 8.7, persvati, 2026-09-20); teeth in tests/acl2/config-stream-tests over a two-group value, with the served TABLE compared at two generations, not only the predicate. Status 2026-09-20 (w11/owner-config): books/owner-config's two open keystones are CLOSED, neither weakened -- each gained the hypothesis (fn-ocfg-statep oc), which is the carried state relation. Closing the first needed one new conjunct of fn-own-relation, fn-own-ids-below-next-p (every open connection's identifier is strictly below fn-own-next-id); the bound was already true of every reachable owner state and merely unstated, so it is not an allocation defect. Teeth ship with them in the new tests/acl2/owner-config-tests, whose scenario holds two configurations and two pins at once so no assertion can hold of an empty value. The R5 wire seam is still open: the served port answers LIST ACTIVE from the allocation domain, so fn-ocfg-served-port-answers-list-active-at-the-pin is false and is recorded rather than stated.

proofs.title: The outbound feed offers exactly the peers in scope, and never a loop (K2, outbound half)
proofs.statement: fn-own-feed-target-is-offerable with fn-own-feed-targets-omit-no-offerable-peer: for a feed table the owner carries, the peers one durably accepted article is offered to are exactly the peers of that table whose own configured record has an outbound half, whose outbound wildmat matches one of the article's own Newsgroups names, whose path-identity the article's Path does not already name, and which is not the peer the article arrived from. fn-own-feed-never-offers-a-loop is the loop-freedom half (RFC 5537 section 3.6) and fn-own-feed-target-is-in-scope the scope half; fn-own-feed-accept-touches-only-its-targets and fn-own-feed-accept-never-enqueues-on-the-origin transport both to the table the owner holds, and fn-own-feed-tick-peer-is-the-feed-tick is the subject rule tying one peer's tick to fn-feed-tick-step on that peer's own feed. Covered scope: one article's octets against one table; the hypothesis is the carried recognizer fn-own-feed-tablep. NOT covered: the statement over fn-own-step (books/owner does not admit on this tree) and fn-feedp preservation, which is cited from books/peer-feed-invariants and not restated.
proofs.progress_note: books/owner-feed and tests/acl2/owner-feed-tests are CERTIFIED as of 2026-09-20, lane w6/peering-feed-4 (laptop ACL2 8.7, evidence build/lanes/w6-peering-feed-4/build/acl2/certify-20260920T212559Z-13370; the persvati closure run-20260920T211802Z-ba78 reached them for the first time). What unblocked them was books/peer-feed-invariants, which now certifies with no open form. books/owner certifies too. The owner-side statement over fn-own-step is still open, and the reason has moved: books/owner-invariants is open at the :open-peer arm of fn-own-step-preserves-relation, not at the feed.

proofs.title: Provenance is typed, and its wire form is lossless and legacy-compatible
proofs.statement: Every string is an admissible provenance (the :legacy kind), so widening the retention evidence slot from stringp to fn-provp changes no stored value; the rendered form of each typed kind is exactly the string that kind's writer produced before the widening; and a provenance the codec can write is the provenance it reads back from its wire form.
proofs.note: The transit path's DURABLE provenance is not covered: fn-peer-injection-arguments still passes fn-peer-evidence's rendering, and fn-peer-evidence-is-the-legacy-rendering is the equation between the typed record and that string, not evidence that the record reaches the store. books/peer-inbound and books/peer-inbound-invariants have no certificate on dev (blocked on fn-peer-echo-reply-effects-well-formed), so those two events are admitted, not certified, and are not listed here.

proofs.title: AUTHINFO on the served path, and what posting follows (W10)
proofs.statement: fn-auth-gated-command-is-refused-and-not-performed: with authentication required and no authenticated subject, a restricted command's step submits nothing, never offers article mode, leaves the session unchanged and its whole effect list is the single 480 line (RFC 4643 section 2.2). fn-auth-post-without-permission-is-not-offered and its lift fn-auth-step-post-without-permission-is-not-offered: a connection whose posting allowance is false is answered by this book and never offered 340, so no body can follow and no submission can leave; fn-auth-postingp is the authenticated principal's credential flag, so a principal enrolled without it is refused 440 however permissive the pinned injection configuration is (RFC 3977 6.3.1.1). fn-served-dispatch-of-a-refused-post-leaves-the-wire-in-place carries that to the served dispatcher: the wire is not switched into article mode and the read carries no submission. fn-auth-pass-before-user-is-482, fn-auth-failed-pass-leaves-the-session-unauthenticated and fn-auth-protected-only-refuses-authinfo-before-tls are the three RFC 4643 section 2.3.2 codes, each with the session unchanged or cleared. fn-auth-pass-accepts-only-a-checking-secret says the accepting branch ran fn-authsec-checkp against the stored verifier; it does NOT say a wrong secret fails, which is A-CRYPTO. Covered scope: one served connection over a pinned archive and a pinned AUTHINFO configuration. The subject of the lifts is fn-auth-step, which books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch calls and which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk reaches through fn-own-read and fn-served-step.
proofs.progress_note: books/nntp-auth, books/served, books/owner and books/nntp-auth-invariants ADMIT with zero errors under tools/acl2 over the book source (ACL2 8.7, laptop, 2026-09-20); tests/acl2/nntp-auth-tests passes 120 assertions. None of the four is CERTIFIED: the installed certificate cache mixes two origin roots and books/config's certificate names sub-books by absolute path from a root that is not the one loaded, so certify-book refuses below peer-inbound. A farm run over the closure is the certification of record and has not been made. OPEN, OB-AUTH-FOLD: the fold-level statement -- no read of a connection under a configuration that grants posting to no one emits a submission -- is not proved. It needs three lemmas that do not exist: fn-auth-step-preserves-the-config (books/nntp-auth), a wire lemma that command mode emits only (:command ...) events (books/wire-invariants), and a reader lemma that fn-nntp-post-step emits a submission only from an (:article ...) event (books/nntp-post). Named in the header of books/nntp-auth-invariants.lisp. Live evidence: planning/evidence/auth-w10-2026-09-20.md, 8 passed 1 skipped; the skip is nntplib, removed from the standard library in Python 3.13, so the independent-client half is NOT supplied.

proofs.title: The recovery window's crash image is kernel-admissible and risks no acknowledged record
proofs.statement: In the recovery window -- the phases between a process replaying what it scanned from the view and completing its five recovery fences -- a crash may drop the record the replay read, because that record's directory entry is the entry operation a dead process left pending. fn-sf-recovery-crash-imagep admits exactly that image and no other, gated by an empty success history; every image it admits is produced by fn-sf-image-crash with the same frontier, records, :replaying phase and success history; and an acknowledged pair of the pre-crash state names a record of EVERY image it admits, the rolled-back one included.
proofs.note: Decision D14-b, lane w10/kernel-freedom. The recognizer is a SECOND one: fn-sf-crash-imagep is unchanged and stays the reliance predicate that fn-own-reopen gates on and every reopen theorem takes as a premise, because widening it is false for the composition -- an owner reopened on an image is a recovery-window state whose own success history is empty while its ledger names records earlier processes acknowledged, and which of a state's records are fenced is a fact about the byte store's pending list, not about the kernel state. The counterexample is mechanized in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp (the owner half) and tests/acl2/store-observed-traces-tests.lisp (the kernel half).
